sections.h2: Fewer than half of producer applications have cleared registration

chart.title: Only 119 of 252 producer applications have been granted
chart.sub: Producer applications on the CPCB Used Oil EPR Portal, 10 August 2026.
chart.source: CPCB Used Oil EPR Portal, accessed 10 August 2026.

sections.means: Fewer than half of the 252 producer applications had been granted by 10 August 2026, more than two years into the obligation period.
sections.todo: Producers with incomplete applications should finish them on the portal, since 94 are marked that way.

sections.h2: EPR certificates cover about 3% of the 2024-25 target

chart.title: Certificates issued so far are about 3% of the first year's target
chart.sub: EPR certificates issued by 5 March 2026, as a share of the 2024-25 used-oil target of 68,946 tonnes.
chart.source: PIB, Parliament answer on EPR status, 5 March 2026; CPCB.

sections.means: About 2,000 tonnes of certificates had been issued by 5 March 2026, against a first-year obligation of 68,946 tonnes.
sections.todo: Recyclers should reconcile recycled tonnage with certificates, since the Parliament answer does not explain the gap.

sections.h2: Lube oil imports rise each year while exports stay small

chart.title: Imports climbed to 3,177 thousand tonnes while exports fell to 11
chart.sub: LOBS/Lube oil line, fiscal years 2023-24 to 2025-26 (2025-26 provisional), thousand tonnes.
chart.source: PPAC, Import/Export of Crude Oil and Petroleum Products (LOBS/Lube oil line), accessed 10 August 2026.

sections.means: Imports ran from 2,412 to 3,177 thousand tonnes a year across 2023-24 to 2025-26, while exports stayed between 11 and 17 thousand tonnes.
sections.todo: Check the provisional 2025-26 PPAC figures against final data before drawing a trade conclusion.

sections.h2: The recycling target climbs in steps to 50% from 2030-31

chart.title: The required recycled share rises from 5% to 50% of oil sold two years earlier
chart.sub: Used-oil recycling target by obligation year, as a percentage of base oil and lubricating oil.
chart.source: CPCB, FAQs on EPR for Used Oil Management, reproducing Rule 27(2), Second Amendment Rules, 2023.

sections.means: The obligation starts at 5% in 2024-25 and reaches 50% from 2030-31 onward, in steps set by Rule 27(2).
sections.todo: Producers and importers should plan purchases of EPR certificates against these steps, since each year's target rises.
